findings.title: A sensitive benefit's title still reaches readers who get 404 on the benefit, through the executive ask that the blocker escalation copies from its corrective case
findings.reproduction: Candidate 4b84bf20 (source 654e39d89), disposable clone and PostgreSQL 16.15. Probe apps/api/test/integration/zz-domain/dom-r4-sensitive-escalation.test.ts (copy in docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/domain/round-4/probes/dom-r4-sensitive-escalation.test.ts.txt). Run: QA_PG_PORT=29802 MTH_PORT_POOL=29800-29809 tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project integration <probe>. Setup, all SYNTHETIC: seedClosureWorld plus the default business calendar; BO creates benefit B01 'Synthetic churn reduction'; a worker-style benefit_variance corrective case names it, titled with the benefit's title as the shipped corrective consumer does (apps/worker/src/handlers/raid.ts line 535: title: benefit.title); the TO marks the benefit sensitive. The TO creates a forum. TL creates and starts two meetings and records the case as a red blocker in both (POST .../meetings/{m}/blocker-statuses {sourceRecordType:'corrective_case', sourceRecordId:<case>, rag:'red'}). The probe then delivers the outbox messages to the worker's real consumer handleBlockerEscalation (apps/worker/src/handlers/escalations.ts). Then, as TL, AUD and SP (none admitted to the benefit), and as TO (the control), read GET /benefits/{id}, GET /executive-decisions, GET /executive-decisions/{askId} and GET /me/inbox.
findings.expected: ADR-0051 §2: a sensitive record a principal is not admitted to is absent from lists, search, exports and assistant retrieval, and its GET is 404. The 2026-11-04 amendment extends this to the rows that carry its values. Its 'Service principals' paragraph adds that a job never reads a sensitive record unless ADR-0053 declares an exception. REQ-S10-002: 'a sensitive benefit is hidden from a workstream member without the grant'. M0188: permissions are enforced on the server for records, APIs, exports and search. After BE-Z4, TL and AUD get 404 on the case itself. The executive ask that the escalation job creates from that case should therefore not carry the case's (that is, the benefit's) title to them. The ask, or at least its 'decision' text and the owner's notification parameters, should be redacted for a reader who is not admitted, or the job should title the ask neutrally (for example by the case code). It is also questionable that TL, who gets 404 on the case, can record a blocker status that names it (201).
findings.actual: Control: TL and AUD get 404 on the benefit and on the case (BE-Z4 works). TL's two blocker statuses naming the restricted case are accepted (201 each). The consumer then returns {outcome:'ask_created'} and creates executive ask DEC-01 with decision = 'Synthetic churn reduction', the sensitive benefit's title, plus blockerRecordType 'corrective_case' and blockerRecordId <case>. TL, AUD and SP all get 200 on GET /executive-decisions, and the list contains the benefit title. They also get 200 on GET /executive-decisions/{id}, whose field 'decision' holds the title. SP, the ask's owner, also receives an inbox notification governance.task.executive_decision_due with messageParams {code:'DEC-01', title:'Synthetic churn reduction'}. The inbox redaction does not apply, because the link names the executive decision. The probe's two expect.soft assertions fail, for TL and AUD, which is the intended red (probe-sensitive-escalation.log, exit 1 by design). By code reading, the ask's title is also indexed by search (apps/worker/src/search/documents.ts: decision spec over title), so the title would also be findable by text. I did not run the search indexer for this. The trigger needs only one person with meeting.prepare who records the case as a red blocker in N consecutive cycles (N = 2 by default). That can be the owner, legitimately, or TL, who learns the case id from the action register, where the case's actions show correctiveCaseId (BE-Z4's residual). The disclosure is of a sensitive benefit's title to every transformation reader.

history.note: Raised in DG6 round 4 by domain-reviewer while verifying F-DG6-220 adversarially. High and mandatory (access control, REQ-S10-002, M0188). This is a different path from F-DG6-220, whose own scope is repaired and verified. Suggested repair, for the architect and backend to decide: (1) the blocker escalation titles an ask about a corrective case of a sensitive benefit neutrally (for example by the case code), or the executive-decision presenters, the notification parameters and the search document redact 'decision' for a reader who is not admitted to the blocker's restricted case; (2) blocker-status writes naming a corrective case apply the same reach check as the case's own routes (404 for a non-admitted caller); (3) sweep the other worker jobs that copy a blocker's or a child's text into another record for the same pattern; (4) add a negative test (TL, AUD, SP) and a positive one (TO, BO).

findings.title: The connector edit screen shows 'Choose…' in the required 'Target transformation' select when the stored target is a transformation the administrator cannot list
findings.reproduction: Candidate 4b84bf20, production-initialized stack apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh, probe e2e/zz-domain/dom-r4-screens.spec.ts (copy in probes/dom-r4-screens.spec.ts.txt), en and ar. dev.lead creates a transformation. dev.admin creates a test_adapter kpi_actual connector targeting it through the API, then opens Administration > Integrations > the connector > Edit.
findings.expected: REQ-S17-001: connectors record their mappings and targets, and the owner can see them. An edit screen should show the stored target, or, when the administrator cannot read that transformation, say so (for example 'A transformation you cannot view' with its code or id). It should not look as if the required field were empty.
findings.actual: The select reads 'Choose…' / 'اختر...' (screenshots dom-r4-connector-unbound-secret.png, en and ar). ConnectorFormPage keeps the stored id in its state and sends it unchanged on save, so nothing is lost and the PUT carries the right target. But the options come from useAllTransformations, which lists only what dev.admin can read. A technical administrator who lacks transformation.read by design (ADR-0051 §7) therefore sees a required field that looks unset, and cannot tell which transformation the feed writes to. If they open the select, they cannot choose the original value again. The effect is a misleading display only: no wrong value is stored, and RAG, approvals and state are not affected.

history.note: Raised in DG6 round 4 by domain-reviewer, answering the D-211 open question on the 'Target transformation' select. Low, not blocking on its own. Suggested repair: when the stored targetTransformationId is not among the options, render an extra option for it ('A transformation you cannot view' plus its id), selected and disabled.
